claims.text: The `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct, enforced entirely within Pulumi and never sent to the cloud provider.
Many cloud resources carry their own, separate deletion-protection attributes that the cloud provider enforces independently of anything Pulumi knows about.
GCP Cloud SQL instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute.
AWS RDS instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute.
A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi and still refuse to delete due to a cloud-provider-level deletion-protection attribute.
A resource can be protected in Pulumi while its cloud-provider-level deletion-protection attribute allows deletion (or vice versa, deletion can succeed despite Pulumi protection being absent).

The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/#deletion-protection-on-the-resource-itself exists and describes how to tell apart Pulumi's `protect` option from a cloud resource's own deletion-protection attribute and how to resolve each.
Pulumi has no single flag to protect every resource in a stack.
Using stack transforms to set the `protect` option on every resource as it's registered applies `protect: true` across the board.
The `protect` resource option guards a resource within Pulumi.
Many cloud resources carry their own, separate deletion-protection attributes that the provider or the cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi's `protect` option.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that the provider or cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi's `protect` option.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that the provider or cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi's `protect` option.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option and a cloud resource's native deletion-protection attribute are complementary layers rather than substitutes for one another.

The 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' section of the destroy-failures troubleshooting page explains how to tell Pulumi's `protect` option apart from a resource's native deletion-protection attribute and how to resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
The `retainOnDelete` resource option takes the opposite approach from `protect`.
The `retainOnDelete` resource option lets Pulumi remove a resource from state without calling the provider's delete operation, leaving the underlying cloud resource in place.
The `retainOnDelete` resource option is the right choice when you want to stop managing a resource with Pulumi, or hand it off, without destroying its data.
A `pulumi destroy` failure is often not an engine problem: the resource itself may be guarded against deletion, and something has to remove that guard before Pulumi can delete it.
Three distinct layers can hold deletion protection on a resource, and the error message usually indicates which layer was hit.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
An error naming a URN and mentioning `protect` indicates the `protect` resource option is the cause, and the fix is described in the Protect documentation page.
Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call at all when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute.
The `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` resource has a `deletionProtection` attribute that, when set, causes the provider to refuse to issue the delete call.
The `gcp.container.Cluster` resource has a `deletionProtection` attribute that, when set, causes the provider to refuse to issue the delete call.
When a provider-enforced deletion-protection attribute blocks a delete, the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
Some cloud APIs reject the delete call themselves, independent of Pulumi.
AWS RDS has a `deletionProtection` attribute enforced at the cloud-API level.
AWS EC2 has a `disableApiTermination` attribute enforced at the cloud-API level.
Azure Resource Manager management locks are a cloud-API-enforced protection independent of Pulumi.
When a cloud-API-enforced protection blocks a delete, the error text comes back from the cloud provider's API, often with a distinct error code such as `ScopeLocked`.
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is already recorded in the stack's state, not what the program currently specifies.

Setting a deletion-protection attribute to `false` in the program alone is not sufficient to allow a subsequent `pulumi destroy` to succeed, for provider-enforced or cloud-API-enforced protection cases.

Setting the deletion-protection attribute to `false` in the Pulumi program, then running `pulumi up`, then running `pulumi destroy` is the correct remediation sequence for provider- or cloud-API-enforced deletion protection.
Running `pulumi up` after changing the deletion-protection attribute propagates the change to both the live resource and Pulumi's state.
If deletion protection was already disabled outside of Pulumi (e.g., directly in the cloud console), running `pulumi refresh` synchronizes the stack's state with reality.
After a `pulumi refresh` synchronizes state following an out-of-band disabling of deletion protection, `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without needing an intervening `pulumi up`.
The GCP `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` resource's `deletionProtection` attribute is provider-enforced.
The GCP `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` resource has a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
The GCP `gcp.container.Cluster` resource's `deletionProtection` attribute is provider-enforced.
The GCP `gcp.bigquery.Table` resource's `deletionProtection` attribute is provider-enforced.
The GCP `gcp.bigquery.Dataset` resource has a `deleteContentsOnDestroy` attribute.
Destroying a `gcp.bigquery.Dataset` that still contains tables fails unless `deleteContentsOnDestroy` is set to `true`.
The `aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` resources have a `deletionProtection` attribute enforced by the AWS API.
The `deletionProtection` attribute on `aws.rds.Instance` / `aws.rds.Cluster` defaults to `false`.
The `aws.s3.BucketV2` resource has a `forceDestroy` attribute.
The `forceDestroy` attribute on `aws.s3.BucketV2` defaults to `false`.
A non-empty `aws.s3.BucketV2` bucket fails to delete unless `forceDestroy` is set to `true`.
The `aws.ec2.Instance` resource has a `disableApiTermination` attribute enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
The `aws.dynamodb.Table` resource has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute enforced by the AWS API.
The `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute on `aws.dynamodb.Table` defaults to `false`.
Any Azure resource under a management lock is protected via `azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and its scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel`.
Azure management locks are enforced by Azure Resource Manager.
A `CanNotDelete` Azure management lock must be removed before the locked resource can be deleted, independent of anything in the Pulumi program.
The `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` resource supports soft delete and purge protection.
Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it.
Recreating an Azure Key Vault with the same name fails with a `VaultAlreadyExists` error until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered.
Purge protection on an Azure Key Vault prevents purging the vault until its retention period elapses.
